title: Erdős Problem #417: Counting Totient Values
description: Does the limit V(x)/V'(x) exist, where V'(x) counts distinct totients from inputs at most x and V(x) counts all totient values at most x?

meta.author: Erdős (1979, 1998)
originalContributions: Defined V'(x) and V(x) counting functions for totient values
Stated three OPEN questions about V(x)/V'(x) ratio
Proved 1 and p-1 (prime p) are totient values
Proved powers of 2 are totient values via φ(2^(k+1)) = 2^k
Characterized odd numbers > 1 as non-totient values

overview.historicalContext:
Erdős first posed this problem in [Er79e], asking about two natural counting functions for Euler's totient values. Given the set of all totient values, one can count how many appear among outputs of small inputs (V'(x)) versus how many totient values exist up to x regardless of input size (V(x)). The question is whether these two counts grow at comparable rates.

The problem was revisited in Erdős and Graham [ErGr80] in their influential monograph on combinatorial number theory. In [Er98], Erdős went further and conjectured that V(x)/V'(x) may actually tend to infinity, suggesting that the vast majority of totient values at most x come from inputs much larger than x. This would be a striking statement about the structure of the totient function's range.

The problem remains open and connects to deep questions about the distribution of totient values. It is known that V(x) ~ cx/log(x) for a constant c (the density of totient values among all integers decays logarithmically), but the relationship between V(x) and V'(x) requires understanding how totient values are generated by inputs of different sizes. Related questions appear in Problem #416, which concerns the structure of the totient range more directly.
overview.problemStatement: Let $V'(x) = |\{\varphi(m) : 1 \le m \le x\}|$ count the distinct totient values achievable from inputs at most $x$, and let $V(x) = |\{n \le x : n = \varphi(m) \text{ for some } m\}|$ count all totient values at most $x$. Does $\lim_{x \to \infty} V(x)/V'(x)$ exist? Is it $> 1$? Erdős conjectured it may be $\infty$.
overview.proofStrategy: The formalization defines both counting functions V'(x) and V(x) using Finset operations on the range of Mathlib's Nat.totient. The IsTotientValue predicate captures membership in the totient range. We prove the trivial inequality V'(x) ≤ V(x), characterize which numbers are totient values (odd numbers > 1 are excluded, all powers of 2 and prime predecessors are included), and state the three open questions using Mathlib's Filter.Tendsto for limits and Filter.atTop for asymptotic behavior.
keyInsights: **Trivial Inequality**: V'(x) ≤ V(x) since every totient from m ≤ x is also a totient value ≤ x, but V(x) may include totients from large m > x
**Parity Obstruction**: Odd numbers > 1 are never totient values because φ(m) is even for m > 2 (and φ(1) = φ(2) = 1), so only even numbers and 1 can be totients
**Powers of 2**: All powers of 2 are totient values via φ(2^(k+1)) = 2^k, providing an infinite family of totient values achievable from specific inputs
**Prime Predecessors**: For any prime p, p-1 is a totient value since φ(p) = p-1, connecting the totient range to the distribution of primes
**Erdős's Conjecture**: The conjecture V(x)/V'(x) → ∞ means most totient values ≤ x arise from inputs m > x, since φ can be small for large m (e.g., φ(2^k) = 2^(k-1))

conclusion.summary: Erdős Problem #417 investigates the ratio V(x)/V'(x) of two counting functions for totient values. V'(x) counts distinct totients achievable from inputs at most x, while V(x) counts all totient values at most x. The trivial bound V'(x) ≤ V(x) holds, but whether the ratio converges, exceeds 1, or tends to infinity as Erdős conjectured in 1998 remains completely open.
conclusion.implications: Understanding this ratio would reveal how efficiently small inputs generate the totient value range versus contributions from large inputs. A resolution would connect to the density of totient values (known to be ~cx/log x) and the multiplicative structure of Euler's totient function.
openQuestions: Is V(x)/V'(x) strictly > 1 for all sufficiently large x?
Does V(x)/V'(x) → ∞ as Erdős conjectured in [Er98]?
What is the precise asymptotic relationship between V(x) and V'(x)?
How does the distribution of totient values from large inputs m > x compare to those from small inputs?
